summary: Executed the selected bypass test in an in-process fixture (no network listener). Recipe: construct a minimal app with the middleware under default configuration and three routes behavior (safe home, protected submit); request the safe route with a fresh client and record the issued cookie; repeat the safe request with that cookie and record the rotated cookie; then send the protected request from a fresh client with the suspected constant as both extracted token and cookie, and a control with an attacker-chosen unknown value. Observed: first safe response issued a random UUID-style cookie; the repeat visit rotated the cookie to the fixed one-character placeholder constant; the fresh-client constant request was ACCEPTED (success status with the protected handler body) while the unknown-value control was rejected with the forbidden status; the original victim token remained accepted. A session-backed configuration blocked the fresh-client constant request, but the probe read only the first cookie header there, so the session path's collapse after a victim's repeat visit stayed unresolved. This supports the constant-collapse mechanism with a discriminating local causal result including controls; it is not an official harness result. Limits: one fixture configuration per check, in-process transport only.
next_hint: The bypass is confirmed for the memory backend and the collapse mechanism lives in the handler re-using the looked-up stored value as the token. Determine the minimal API-compatible repair that also covers the session backend and every extraction source, and which regression matrix (extraction-source variants, single-use mode, cross-client ownership, upstream suite, all-accept countercheck) discriminates a real repair from one that merely hides the cookie collapse.
